example: Two sibling declarations named `run` in one file, guarded by different `#[cfg]` attributes, have selectors `fn[run]#1` and `fn[run]#2` in source order. Their source line numbers are not part of either selector. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
rationale:
The example is covered by passing-style tests that match its scenario and expected outcomes.

**Implementation.** `disambiguate` in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/mod.rs` (lines 623–651) groups sibling nodes by their base segment, such as `fn[run]`. When a group has more than one member, it appends `#N`, numbering from 1 in child order, which is source order. The segment text contains no line information, so line numbers are not part of any selector.

**Tests.** Three tests reference `selector_duplicate_names`:
- `duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers` (`crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/tests.rs` 903–935) is the direct test.
  - It uses two sibling `fn run` items guarded by `#[cfg(a)]` and `#[cfg(b)]`.
  - It asserts the selectors are exactly `["fn[run]#1", "fn[run]#2"]`.
  - It checks that `#1` is the first declaration in the file, using byte offsets.
  - It swaps the two declarations and confirms the ordinals swap, so the ordinal follows source order.
  - It prefixes three blank lines, which moves the line numbers (`line_start` becomes 4). The selectors and the structural hash of `#1` stay unchanged, so line numbers are not part of the selector.
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` (35–100) covers `fn[repeated]#1` and `fn[repeated]#2` for cfg-guarded siblings. It also checks that each selector resolves back to its own node and that the bare `fn[repeated]` is rejected as ambiguous.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` (662–706) covers the same cfg-guarded duplicates alongside other item kinds.

**Gaps.** I found none. The cited requirement `rust_item_selectors` is context only and is not reassessed.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
